stem: A Massachusetts prescription was written on 1 March. A patient presents it and the pharmacist must decide whether it is still within a thirty-day window. Which date is the last day on which it remains within date?

choices.text: 30 March, counting 1 March as day one of the period.
31 March, counting 2 March as day one of the period.
1 April, because a partial first day is disregarded entirely.
29 March, because both the first and the last day are excluded.
It cannot be determined without knowing the schedule of the drug.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(10) provides that in order to determine whether a prescription is within date a pharmacist shall count THE DAY AFTER THE PRESCRIPTION WAS WRITTEN AS DAY ONE. With 1 March as the date written, 2 March is day one, so day thirty is 31 March.

choice_analysis.A: That counts the date of issue as day one, which the regulation excludes.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: day one is 2 March, so the thirtieth day is 31 March.
choice_analysis.C: The regulation fixes the start precisely rather than disregarding a day.
choice_analysis.D: Only the date written is excluded, not the final day.
choice_analysis.E: The counting convention is general and does not vary by schedule.

related_facts: The length of the window is set by the provision governing that drug
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates start counting on the date the prescription was written, which shifts every boundary by a day.

reasoning_steps: Apply the counting convention to fix day one
Count forward the length of the period
Note that the convention does not vary by schedule
